title: the WSG first aid equipment slice - the bandage, splint, stretcher and litter gear rules with the carry and terrain semantics, printed p. 71
audit_label: R481 WSG first aid equipment pin audit
audit_comment: The first aid equipment rules: bandages (several swatches of clean fabric for covering and binding wounds and burns; clothing torn into strips works in a pinch but adventurers clothing is usually not clean, leaving a possibility of infection even when the wound is bandaged), splints (not necessary when traveling through a wooded area, but wise to pack for a mountain climb or a desert crossing: a couple of straight, short 2-3-foot pieces of wood or other rigid material bound along the sides of a broken limb to keep the bones properly aligned; a large piece of thick leather or untanned hide works too, if large and rigid enough to keep the limb and the joints on both sides immobilized, in the same manner as a plaster cast), the stretcher (parts carried separately and assembled when needed: two poles at least as long as the injured character height, sturdy cloth or leather large enough to recline on, and rope or cord of sufficient length to bind the poles to the edges; two comrades can carry the victim as long as each supports half the weight without being too encumbered to move), and the litter (essentially a stretcher plus extra rope or cord to bind the victim to the frame; one character - or one mount or beast of burden - can transport the bound victim, supporting half the weight; unwise over rugged or very rugged terrain because one end always drags on the ground and the victim is jostled as the litter skids and bumps; the DM may rule the trip causes further damage from the rough handling).

banner.title: R481: the WSG FIRST AID EQUIPMENT slice, printed p. 71 - the eleventh camping-arc round and the LAST of the medicine chapter, a pure prose round with NO table: the four essentials - bandages, splints, stretcher and litter - with the party gear-advice frame (nobody goes through an adventure unscathed, so pack the materials for administering aid to the injured).
banner.provenance: The settle: two-way clean on the first pass - the tesseract full-text read and the pdfy layout read agree on every number of the section (the 2-3 foot splint length, the two-pole stretcher, the half-weight carry bars), and the tsv confirms the geometry cell by cell; no contested cells, no vision reads needed. The skin ailments and other-injuries prose at the top of the page belongs to the injuries chapter landed at R480 and stays out of scope here.
banner.sentinel: Bounds held: the splint length runs 2-3 feet; both carry bars use one-half of the victim weight - two carriers on a stretcher, one on a litter.

bools.name: wfePartyPacksAidMaterials
bools.comment: it is a good idea for the party gear to include the materials for administering aid to the injured in the line of duty

bools.name: wfeBandagesCleanFabric
bools.comment: at least one backpack should contain several swatches of clean fabric for covering and binding wounds and burns

bools.name: wfeClothingStripsInPinch
bools.comment: in a pinch an article of clothing torn into strips can be used for bandages

bools.name: wfeClothingCarriesInfection
bools.comment: an adventurer clothing is usually not clean, so infection remains possible even when the wound is bandaged

bools.name: wfeSplintsUnneededInWood
bools.comment: splints may be unnecessary when the journey passes through a wooded area

bools.name: wfeSplintsPackedForMountainDesert
bools.comment: for a mountain climb or a desert crossing it is wise to pack a couple of straight, short rigid pieces bound along the sides of a broken limb to keep the bones properly aligned

bools.name: wfeLeatherHideAsSplint
bools.comment: a large piece of thick leather or untanned hide works as a splint if large and rigid enough to immobilize the limb and the joints on both sides, like a plaster cast

bools.name: wfeStretcherPartsCarriedSeparately
bools.comment: most groups carry the stretcher parts separately and assemble the stretcher if and when it is needed

bools.name: wfeStretcherPolesAsTallAsVictim
bools.comment: the poles must be at least as long as the injured character height

bools.name: wfeStretcherNeedsSurfaceAndBinding
bools.comment: sturdy cloth or leather large enough to recline on, plus rope or cord of sufficient length to bind the poles to the edges

bools.name: wfeStretcherTwoCarryHalfEach
bools.comment: two comrades can carry the victim as long as each supports half the weight without being too encumbered to move

bools.name: wfeLitterSameAsStretcher
bools.comment: the litter is essentially the same as a stretcher, except extra rope or cord binds the victim to the frame

bools.name: wfeLitterOneCarrierOrBeast
bools.comment: one character, mount or beast of burden can transport the bound victim while supporting half the weight

bools.name: wfeLitterUnwiseOnRugged
bools.comment: it is usually not wise to transport a litter over rugged or very rugged terrain

bools.name: wfeLitterDragsAndJostles
bools.comment: one end of the litter is always on the ground and the victim is jostled as it skids and bumps along

bools.name: wfeDmMayRuleRoughHandlingDamage
bools.comment: if the victim must be kept motionless, the DM may rule that a rugged trip causes further damage from the rough handling

8089f20..414dbb3), the WSG INJURIES AND TREATMENT slice,
printed p. 70 - the tenth camping-arc round, a pure
prose round with NO table: the five specific injuries
and treatments pinned as rules/wsginj.h with the include
after wsglore.h at line 185 (prefix wtr, free in all four
files). The frame: first-aid skills are common knowledge,
useful only when the DM rules with proper reason that a
specific injury was suffered. The broken bone: the splint
aligns the ends, no hp regained until splinted, use of
the injured extremity costs an immediate 1d6 and
neutralizes healing to date, the bone heals last. The
minor burn: two turns of immersion or a tight clean
cloth for normal 1-per-day healing, else the -1 pain
penalty and half-speed healing. The major burn: more
than half the body, rest until half the lost hp,
voluntary activity forfeits all regained points plus 1d4
per round, the -3 pain penalty (exactly three times the
minor one), the victim can still be carried. The major
wound: an edged melee weapon with an unmodified damage
roll of 6 or higher, DM discretion or the 25% artery
chance, 2-4 (1d3+1) hp per round of bleeding, direct
pressure for 2-7 (1d6+1) rounds at 1 hp lost per round,
wrapping halts but a healing-proficiency character is
needed for recovery, early release negates. The minor
wound: assumed bandaged at first opportunity. THE
